# GitLab

Connect GitLab.com or a self-managed GitLab instance. Each account saves its exact instance origin. Use a separate account for each instance.

## OAuth

GitLab.com uses the hosted OAuth client when it is configured. For a self-managed instance, create a confidential OAuth application on that instance. Set its callback to the URL shown on the connection form, enable authorization-code and refresh-token access, and request the api and read_user scopes. Enter that instance's client ID and secret when you connect. The api scope already includes read_user.

## Access tokens

Create a personal, project, or group access token on the selected instance. Use api for full access or read_api for read-only access. The app sends the token in the PRIVATE-TOKEN header only to the saved instance. Mutating tools still require approval.

## Instance origins

Enter the HTTPS origin without a path. A private origin needs an exact entry in EXECUTOR_URL_ALLOW_HTTP_ORIGINS on the deployment and network access from the tools service. This setting does not allow sibling hosts or ports. Redirects to origins outside the deployment policy are refused.
